title: Practice: Ordering, Honeybee Total, and Extending Sequences
description: Interactive number line tool for CBSE Grade 7 Mathematics (Decimals chapter). The tool presents a horizontal number line from 0 to 45 with tenth-level granularity. Students drag four labelled tokens — 4/10, 4 1/10, 41/10, and 41 1/10 — to their correct positions. The tool highlights when two tokens overlap (4 1/10 and 41/10 both equal 4.1) with a special 'Same value!' badge. After correct placement, the ordering statement '4/10 < 4 1/10 = 41/10 < 41 1/10' appears. A second tab provides six sequences where students drag the next four terms onto a number line segment, seeing the common difference pattern visually. Feedback is immediate with green/red indicators.
chapter: Chapter 3 — A Peek Beyond the Point
subject: Mathematics
instructions_for_student: Drag each of the four values to the correct position on the number line. Convert all to one-tenths first. Did you notice two values land at the same spot? Which ones and why?
teaching_notes: Use AFTER students have attempted the ordering exercise on paper. The number line reveals that 4 1/10 and 41/10 are the same value (4.1), which surprises many students. After the ordering section, switch to sequence extension mode for the six sequences.

Discover that 4 1/10 (mixed number) and 41/10 (improper fraction) represent the same decimal value 4.1

Identify arithmetic sequence patterns with decimal common differences
Extend both increasing and decreasing decimal sequences
Calculate the total length of a honeybee's body using addition of tenths
